label.summary: Claims address the US relationship with Israel, emphasizing its security and right to defend itself. Multiple claims also reference a two-state solution involving both Israel and Palestine, with varying emphasis on justice and the conditions for achieving peace. Positions range from unconditional support for Israel to calls for a just resolution and diplomatic efforts.
label.title: Israeli-Palestinian Conflict and US Policy Positions

claims.claim_text: The United States should stand with Israel against those who seek its destruction.

The Israeli state has a right to defend its people, but after more than 60 years of self-defense and 40 years of an unjust occupation of the West Bank and Gaza, it should be self-evident that peace and security for Israel cannot be achieved by injustice towards another people.
Israel must have secure, defensible borders.
The United States must help Israel identify and strengthen those partners who are truly committed to peace, while isolating those who seek conflict and instability.
America supports the vision of two democratic states living in peace and security: Israel, with Jerusalem as its capital, and Palestine.

Democratic Socialists of America urges the U.S. government and the international community to ensure that the temporary ceasefire in Gaza leads to a sustained diplomatic effort to negotiate a just, two-state solution to the conflict between the Palestinian and Israeli peoples.
